cur:monumental-san-raising-of-lazarus.summary: Lazarus, still wrapped in his grave-clothes, stands in the doorway of a small temple-like tomb at the top of a flight of steps, as Christ, haloed and in purple, stretches out his hand to call him forth, a disciple at his side. Unlike the catacomb paintings, Christ here commands with a gesture rather than a wand.
facts: The thirteen scenes of the north wall show Christ's miracles and teaching; in all of them he appears young and beardless, robed in imperial purple.
The Raising of Lazarus, read near the end of Lent before Holy Week, was one of the most frequently depicted miracles in Early Christian art.
The scenes were not arranged in biblical order but are thought to follow the Gospel readings of the Lenten liturgy in Theodoric's palace church.
